statement: Create a terrain model from contour curves or elevation curves, producing a surface that passes through every contour at its stated elevation.
superiority: Dino 8 should build the terrain natively with exact contour interpolation and a deviation report, with no licence needed.

acceptance.corpus: Synthetic Gaussian hill z=50*exp(-r^2/400) sampled as 5 m contours
acceptance.tolerance: Terrain elevation at 1000 random points within 0.25 m of analytic z; contour elevations reproduced within 1e-6

notes: Vendor site (asuni.com) was unreachable; row is based on McNeel-hosted descriptions.

statement: Create a terrain from survey sources: point clouds, DEM raster files and web-imported elevation, with thinning and boundary clipping.

source.ref: Terrain from point cloud / DEM / web import

superiority: Dino 8 should stream large rasters and clouds with level-of-detail meshing so a 10 million-point site stays interactive.

acceptance.corpus: USGS 1/3 arc-second DEM tile (OGC GeoTIFF) 10 x 10 km clipped to a 2 km site
acceptance.tolerance: Mesh vertex elevations within 0.5 m of raster; area of clipped boundary equals the polygon area within 0.1 percent

notes: Vendor site (asuni.com) was unreachable; row is based on McNeel-hosted descriptions.

statement: Apply cut and fill to a terrain from a platform, terrace, pond or embankment shape, with slope rules, and update the terrain surface from the Grasshopper component.
superiority: Dino 8 should apply cut and fill as a non-destructive, undoable terrain operation with slope-limited transitions.

acceptance.corpus: Flat 20 x 20 m platform at z=0 cut into a 5 percent plane slope with 1:3 side slopes
acceptance.tolerance: Platform elevation exact within 1e-6; side slope within 0.5 percent of 1:3

statement: Carve a path or drainage trench through a terrain along a curve with a given cross-section.
superiority: Dino 8 should keep the trench parametric on its curve and cross-section so edits re-cut the terrain.

acceptance.corpus: Straight 30 m trench, trapezoid section 1 m deep, 0.5 m bottom width
acceptance.tolerance: Trench depth and width within 1 cm of the section along the full length

statement: Compute earthwork volumes and areas for terrain modifications and list cut, fill and net totals by terrain division.
superiority: Dino 8 should compute volumes by exact prismatic integration of both surfaces, with a signed-volume audit and totals that always balance.

acceptance.corpus: Plane z=0 vs plane z=1 over 10 x 10 m, and a cone of known volume pi*r^2*h/3
acceptance.tolerance: Plane case exactly 100 m3; cone volume within 0.1 percent of the closed form

statement: Divide a terrain into zones that carry their own areas, materials and uses, generating zoning and area lists from the divisions.
superiority: Dino 8 should keep zones as a first-class partition with guaranteed no-gap, no-overlap topology and live area tables.

acceptance.corpus: Terrain split into 6 zones by closed curves
acceptance.tolerance: Zone areas sum to the terrain area within 1e-6 relative; no overlaps (pairwise overlap area < 1e-9)

statement: Insert plants from a searchable species database at chosen points, with each plant carrying its botanical data and size.
superiority: Dino 8 should include an open species database with units, growth data and licence-free models, queryable from definitions.

acceptance.corpus: Insert 5 species at 100 points from a table
acceptance.tolerance: 100 plants placed with correct species, height and canopy attributes (exact attribute match)

notes: Vendor site (asuni.com) was unreachable; row is based on McNeel-hosted descriptions. Species count differs by source (1800 and 8000 are both quoted); do not rely on the figure.

statement: Scatter plants over an area or along a curve by density, spacing and species mix, with random variation of size and rotation.

source.ref: Plant distribution over areas and curves

superiority: Dino 8 should place plants with blue-noise sampling and collision rules so canopies never overlap unless asked.

acceptance.corpus: 1000 m2 area, density 0.5 plants per m2, minimum spacing 1.2 m
acceptance.tolerance: Count within 5 percent of 500; no pair closer than 1.2 m; seeded run reproducible

statement: Produce plant lists and quantity take-offs by species, size and zone, exported to a table.
superiority: Dino 8 should keep quantities live-linked to the model and export CSV or XLSX with unit costs.

acceptance.corpus: Model with 300 plants of 12 species in 4 zones
acceptance.tolerance: Counts per species and zone exactly equal the model; totals sum to 300

statement: Switch plants between detailed 3D, low-detail and billboard representations and between 2D symbols, so large plantings stay fast.
superiority: Dino 8 should use GPU instancing and automatic level of detail so 100 000 plants render interactively.

acceptance.corpus: 100 000 plant instances in the viewport
acceptance.tolerance: >= 30 fps orbit on reference GPU; memory < 2 GB

statement: Show seasonal appearance and plant growth over time in renders and animations, such as leaf colour change and size increase by year.
superiority: Dino 8 should drive growth and season from a timeline parameter in the native animation system.

acceptance.corpus: Tree with 5 m height at year 10 and growth curve
acceptance.tolerance: Height at year t equals the curve within 1 percent; four seasonal states render with distinct leaf colours

statement: Explode Lands plants into ordinary meshes inside Grasshopper so they can be used as plain geometry.
superiority: Dino 8 should convert any plant instance to editable geometry in one operation without loading extra definitions.

acceptance.corpus: 20 plants exploded
acceptance.tolerance: Mesh vertex counts and bounding boxes equal the 3D plant representation within 1e-6

notes: The shared explode definition is referenced in a forum thread; details were not fetched.

statement: Create civil landscape elements along curves: paths, stairs, low walls, fences and rows of elements with parametric section.

source.ref: Paths, stairs, dwarf walls, fences, element rows

superiority: Dino 8 should use native parametric hardscape objects with quantity and material data and code-based stair checks.

acceptance.corpus: Path 2 m wide along a 50 m curve; stair with 150 mm risers over 1.2 m rise
acceptance.tolerance: Path area within 0.5 percent of length x width; stair has 8 risers of equal height within 1 mm

statement: Use a library of urban furniture and landscape blocks, generating the 2D plan block automatically from the 3D block.

source.ref: Urban furniture blocks and automatic 2D block

superiority: Dino 8 should auto-generate plan symbols from 3D with line weights following drawing standards.

acceptance.corpus: Bench block 1.8 x 0.5 x 0.45 m
acceptance.tolerance: Generated plan outline bounding box equals 1.8 x 0.5 within 1 mm

statement: Lay out an irrigation system with sprinkler types, sprinkler distributions and pipes, and list the components used.
superiority: Dino 8 should add hydraulic checks (pressure loss, coverage) that the original lacks, so layouts are verified rather than just drawn.

acceptance.corpus: Rectangular 20 x 30 m lawn with 4 m radius sprinklers on a square grid
acceptance.tolerance: Coverage >= 95 percent of area; pipe lengths in the list equal drawn lengths within 1e-6

acceptance.corpus: Single pipe run, 50 mm PVC, 2 L/s, 100 m (Hazen-Williams C=150)
acceptance.tolerance: Pressure loss within 2 percent of the closed-form Hazen-Williams value

notes: Reviews describe the original irrigation tooling as basic; the hydraulics check is a Dino 8 addition.

statement: Generate dynamic 2D technical plans (planting layout, dimension, irrigation) with labels and lists that update when the model changes.
superiority: Dino 8 should keep plans live-linked to the 3D model and plot them to PDF with standards-based line weights and scale.

acceptance.corpus: Planting plan 1:200 of a 40 plant model
acceptance.tolerance: Every plant has a label with the correct species; drawing scale exactly 1:200; update after moving one plant takes < 1 s

statement: Create sections and elevations through terrain, plants and civil elements to document levels and planting heights.
superiority: Dino 8 should generate live section views with terrain profile, plant silhouettes and elevation tags in one step.

acceptance.corpus: Section line across a sloped terrain with 5 trees
acceptance.tolerance: Profile elevations within 0.01 m of the terrain; tree heights in the section equal model heights within 1 cm

notes: No Lands-specific section tool documentation was found; the row reflects the workflow described on the Rhino landscape page and Lands plans feature.

statement: Extract and reverse boundary curves from Lands objects and reference Lands elements as geometry from Grasshopper components.
superiority: Dino 8 should expose every landscape object's geometry and parameters directly to scripts with stable identifiers.

acceptance.corpus: Fence, wall and path objects
acceptance.tolerance: Extracted curve length equals object path length within 1e-6; reversed curve direction opposite

statement: Edit terrain, plants and civil objects from Grasshopper by creating Lands objects from definition data, with the document staying consistent.
superiority: Dino 8 should make the landscape object model native to scripting, with no load-order requirement (Lands must be loaded before Grasshopper, a common failure).

acceptance.corpus: Definition creating 1 terrain, 50 plants, 1 path
acceptance.tolerance: All objects exist after solve; reopening the file yields identical objects

statement: Exchange landscape designs with BIM tools so planting and terrain appear in a building model.
superiority: Dino 8 should export plants and terrain as IFC geographic elements with quantities and classification.

acceptance.corpus: Model with terrain and 50 plants exported to IFC4 and re-imported
acceptance.tolerance: Object counts equal; terrain surface area within 0.1 percent; species attribute preserved
